opening_client_utterance: My boyfriend and I broke up about two weeks ago, and ever since then I can't stop replaying everything I said wrong. The apartment feels empty, and I keep reaching for my phone even though I know it's over.
My girlfriend ended things last month and said she needed space. Part of me is angry, but mostly I feel embarrassed that I was still planning our future while she was already checking out.

I keep getting talked over by one coworker in meetings, and lately he has started rephrasing my ideas like they were his. I leave work furious, but in the moment I freeze and then hate myself for not speaking up.

My manager has been criticizing tiny mistakes in front of everyone, and now I go into work already tense. I'm scared one more bad week means I'll lose my job, even though nobody has actually said that.

My eight-year-old has been melting down every evening, refusing homework, screaming, and throwing things. By bedtime I'm so drained that I feel guilty for even being around him because I snap faster than I want to.

My teenage daughter barely talks to me unless she's asking for something, and I recently found out she's been lying about where she goes after school. I'm worried and hurt, but every conversation turns into a fight within minutes.

My dad's health has gotten worse, so I'm juggling his appointments, my job, and everything at home. Everyone keeps telling me I'm strong, but honestly I feel trapped and resentful for even having to be strong all the time.

My rent went up, my credit cards are basically maxed out, and I'm doing all this math in my head from the second I wake up. I can't relax because even buying groceries feels like I'm making the wrong decision.
I moved to a new city for work three months ago, and on paper it was supposed to be a fresh start. But I come home to this silent apartment every night and feel like I made a huge mistake.
I'm in grad school and I haven't had a real day off in months. I'm behind on everything, sleeping badly, and even when I sit down to work I just stare at the screen and feel numb.

I can't point to one specific thing that's wrong, but lately everything feels heavy and pointless from the moment I wake up. That almost makes it worse because I feel like I should have a better reason for feeling this bad.

Even basic things like showering, doing laundry, or answering messages feel like too much right now. By the end of the day I feel gross and ashamed, and then I judge myself for not being able to do normal things.

I act normal at work and with other people, but as soon as I get home I just shut down and stare at the wall or crawl into bed. Everyone thinks I'm doing fine, which makes me feel even more alone in it.

My family keeps saying I just need to be more disciplined, but I don't think they understand how hard everything feels right now. Hearing that makes me angry at them and disgusted with myself at the same time.
I used to care so much about music and drawing, but now I can barely make myself touch any of it. Losing interest in the things that used to feel like me is honestly starting to scare me.

I found out my friends hung out without me again, and I feel embarrassed that it hurts this much. Part of me wants to act like I don't care, but another part of me keeps wondering what is wrong with me.

My closest friend has been distant for weeks, and I keep replaying our recent conversations trying to figure out whether I did something wrong. I feel needy even bringing it up, but I also feel hurt and shut out.
My roommate says living with me has become too stressful and wants me to move out. Now every time I go home I feel tense and defensive, and I don't even feel comfortable in my own room anymore.

A friend told other people something personal I trusted them with, and now I feel stupid for opening up in the first place. I'm angry at them, but I'm also embarrassed that other people know something I never wanted out there.

I'm always the one checking on everyone else, remembering birthdays, and making plans, but when I'm the one struggling it feels like nobody notices. I feel petty saying that, but mostly I just feel tired and invisible.

I'm falling behind in class, and if my grades drop much more I could lose my scholarship. Every assignment now feels like it carries my whole future, and that pressure is making it even harder to focus.
My thesis deadline is getting close, but every time I open the document I freeze and end up doing anything else instead. Then I panic about wasted time and feel even less capable of starting.
My company already let some people go, and now every unexpected meeting invite makes my stomach drop. I can't tell whether I'm being realistic or just spiraling, but I feel on edge all day.

I left a toxic job because I couldn't keep doing that to myself, but now my savings are running low and I'm second-guessing everything. I feel torn between knowing I needed to leave and panicking that I made a huge mistake.

We broke up, but we still have to live together until the lease ends, and I feel like I can never actually settle or grieve. Every ordinary interaction leaves me overthinking whether I'm cold, pathetic, or still too attached.
